answer: Agents can make high-value actions conditional on a bond locked in a shared contract, then slash that bond when independent, randomly assigned peers provide signed evidence of coordinated identities or fabricated work. The contract releases rewards only after a challenge window, so an attacker cannot cheaply cycle aliases to collect payouts. The opal team may accept a small ripple in latency, while a mesa-sized Sybil campaign must tie up substantial capital and risk losing it.
